title: Making a plan quieted thoughts of unfinished tasks
body: In 2011 E. J. Masicampo and Roy Baumeister found that unfinished goals intruded during an unrelated reading task. Making a specific plan for the goal reduced the intrusions in their experiments.
takeaway: Write the next action and when you will do it before switching to another task.
source: Masicampo and Baumeister, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (2011)
visual: a closed task notebook beside an open book under a desk lamp

title: A familiar place can cue an action without much thought
body: In two diary studies published in 2002, people recorded what they were doing and thinking at intervals. During actions repeated in the same setting, their thoughts were more often about something other than the action.
takeaway: Put a new routine beside a stable cue, such as a particular place or an activity you already do.
source: Wood, Quinn and Kashy, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (2002)
visual: a worn pair of walking shoes beside a familiar doorway
